rows: Weak label: ‘easy book.’
Operational rule: easy for this reader if difficulty level ≤ 2 and unfamiliar words per page ≤ 3.
Two labelers test the same 8 books.
Agreement of 7/8 identifies one disagreement to review. Check the source, each annotator’s application and the label rule before choosing a repair.

be10c2f296955f7900975cf6de4c5f48de7c08b8.title: Worked evidence for Image Generation Models
rows: In this simplified diffusion-style image generator, begin with random visual noise. Other image-generation methods use different procedures.
At each step, predict a slightly more structured image guided by the prompt.
Learned patterns influence shapes, textures, and relationships.
The result is generated, not retrieved evidence of a real event.

0772e307f7831d4a6c240545a43f92ef42c3ce00.title: Four-step worked evidence for Week 10: Baselines First
rows: Test set has 12 healthy and 8 spotted leaves.
Always-healthy baseline gets 12 ÷ 20 = 60% accuracy but 0% spotted recall.

On the same 20 leaves, the visible-spot rule correctly labels 5 spotted leaves, misses 3 spotted leaves, correctly labels 10 healthy leaves and falsely marks 2 healthy leaves as spotted. Accuracy=(5+10)/20=75%; spotted recall=5/8=62.5%.
A learned model must beat relevant baseline metrics—not only one convenient total.

954aa38afb07f6e414fbafe921f066b9c3ace292.title: Four-step worked evidence for Week 12: Nearest Neighbors
rows: New leaf has normalized features (2, 3).
Using Manhattan distance, add the absolute coordinate differences. Training leaves at (2, 2), (4, 3), and (1, 5) have distances 1, 2, and 3 from (2, 3).
With k=1, nearest label wins; with k=3, majority among all three wins.
Rescale features and retest because centimeters must not overwhelm a 0–1 color score.

8942824ccb50b3bbc88d9772a07f13f4bc8c3659.title: Four-step worked evidence for Week 14: Scores and Calibration Intuition
rows: Each score estimates the probability that the selected label is correct. Ten predictions have such scores near 0.8.
Only six are correct, so observed correctness is 6 ÷ 10 = 60%.
The score ranking may still help, but 0.8 should not be stated as an 80% guarantee.
Use bins across many cases and design an uncertain zone requiring human review.

99a131bc60d8a509c3e1f06ca437c13533379a5b.title: Four-step worked evidence for Week 34: Capstone Dataset and Baseline
rows: Freeze dataset card v3 and grouped split s2 with no plant identity crossing sets.
Test set remains sealed; validation supports model choices.

Validation has 12 healthy and 8 spotted leaves. The always-healthy baseline scores 12/20=60% accuracy and 0/8=0% spotted recall. The rule has TP=5, FN=3, TN=10, FP=2: accuracy 75% and spotted recall 62.5%.
Acceptance requires valid citations, metric calculations, subgroup review, and safe escalation.
